CONF_PARAM_1.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Profiler configuration - Reference day, for PROVOR and ARVOR floats this is: The day number on which the first profile is to be made. The day when the mission starts is zero.

CONF_PARAM_2.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Pressure scrutation period during the pressure activation phase.

CONF_PARAM_3.CONF_PARAM_LABEL: Threshold of pressure to start mission (dbar)
CONF_PARAM_3.CONF_PARAM_DEFINITION: Threshold of pressure to start mission (dbar)
CONF_PARAM_3.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: depth at which float is set to pressure activate

CONF_PARAM_4.CONF_PARAM_LABEL: Maximum number of days before starting mission (days)
CONF_PARAM_4.CONF_PARAM_DEFINITION: Maximum number of days before starting mission (days)
CONF_PARAM_4.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: The pressure activation phase starts after the first successfull auto-test and ends (with the start of the float mission) at the end of the CONFIG_AUX_PressureActivationTimeout_days period. During this phase the float checks the external pressure and can start its mission as soon as a CONFIG_PressureActivation_dbar pressure is measured. At the end of this phase the mission will automatically start.

CONF_PARAM_5.CONF_PARAM_LABEL: Waiting at surface before starting mission (s)
CONF_PARAM_5.CONF_PARAM_DEFINITION: Waiting at surface before starting mission (s)
CONF_PARAM_5.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Float waiting period before the first cycle of its mission (in minutes).

CONF_PARAM_6.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: For APEX and ARVOR floats this is the total duration of one cycle, usually 240 hours (10 days). For SOLO floats this is the total duration of one cycle, assuming that all float operations reach their full time-out intervals before moving to the next float stage. Typically the actual cycle time will be shorter than this value.

CONF_PARAM_8.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: The float performs a telemetry transmission at the end of the cycle (Yes=1/No=0).

CONF_PARAM_9.CONF_PARAM_LABEL: Mode of buoyancy reduction (0: secure, 1: fast)
CONF_PARAM_9.CONF_PARAM_DEFINITION: Mode of buoyancy reduction (0: secure, 1: fast)
CONF_PARAM_9.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Mode of the buoyancy reduction (0: secure, 1: fast).

CONF_PARAM_10.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: park pressure - this may change if the float is reprogrammed and must be reported in the mission configuration settings

CONF_PARAM_11.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Mean descent speed during descent to parking depth.

CONF_PARAM_12.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Minimum duration of the parking drift phase.

CONF_PARAM_13.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Defines the target pressure interval before performing a buoyancy readjustment to reposition during the drift at parking depth. When a PRES measurement (sampled to monitor the float drift at parking depth) is outside the [parking_pressure +- CONFIG_AUX_PressureTargetToleranceBeforeParkDriftReposition_dbar] interval, the float adjusts its buoyancy.

CONF_PARAM_14.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Defines the target pressure interval after a reposition to enter anew in the drift phase at parking depth (in dbars).

CONF_PARAM_15.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: profile pressure - this may change if the float is reprogrammed and must be reported in the mission configuration settings

CONF_PARAM_16.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Mean descent speed during descent to profile depth.

CONF_PARAM_17.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Minimum duration of the profile drift phase.

CONF_PARAM_18.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Defines the target pressure interval before performing a buoyancy readjustment to reposition during the drift at profile depth. When a PRES measurement (sampled to monitor the float drift at parking depth) is outside the [parking_pressure +- CONFIG_AUX_PressureTargetToleranceBeforeProfDriftReposition_dbar] interval, the float adjust its buoyancy.

CONF_PARAM_19.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Defines the target pressure interval for float drift at profile depth (in dbars).

CONF_PARAM_20.CONF_PARAM_LABEL: Expected depth (0 if only 1 ascent phase)
CONF_PARAM_20.CONF_PARAM_DEFINITION: Expected depth (0 if only 1 ascent phase)
CONF_PARAM_20.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Expected depth at end of ascent (0 if only one ascent phase).

CONF_PARAM_21.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: ascent speed during upcast in mm/s or cm/s (can be used to estimate the profile duration)

CONF_PARAM_22.CONF_PARAM_LABEL: Cycle periodicity (1/x where x=number of the cycle)
CONF_PARAM_22.CONF_PARAM_DEFINITION: Cycle periodicity (1/x where x=number of the cycle)
CONF_PARAM_22.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Cycle periodicity of the in air measurement phase: - 0 means no in air acquisition - 1 means in air acquisition every cycle - N means in air acquisition one cycle every N cycles

CONF_PARAM_23.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Duration of the in air measurement phase.

CONF_PARAM_24.CONF_PARAM_LABEL: Waiting at the end of the cycle (s)
CONF_PARAM_24.CONF_PARAM_DEFINITION: Waiting at the end of the cycle (s)
CONF_PARAM_24.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Duration of the waiting period at the end of a cycle.

CONF_PARAM_25.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Period of the Iridium transmission when in End Of Life mode (in minutes).

CONF_PARAM_26.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: First threshold of the buoyancy reduction phase (in dbars). From the surface to this first threshold, the float performs one initial valve action (of a computed duration) and N1 additional valve actions (of fixed durations) until the crossing of this first threshold.

CONF_PARAM_27.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Second threshold of the buoyancy reduction phase (in dbars). From the first threshold to this second threshold, the float performs N2 additional valve actions (of computed durations) until the crossing of this second threshold. The descent to park phase starts at the crossing of this second threshold.

CONF_PARAM_28.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Time delay after each valve action before checking the pressure during the buoyancy reduction phase (in seconds).

CONF_PARAM_29.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Constant oil volume transfered at each valve action during the first step (between surface and first threshold) of the buoyancy reduction phase.

CONF_PARAM_30.CONF_PARAM_LABEL: Tolerance in pressure of expected depth (dbar)
CONF_PARAM_30.CONF_PARAM_DEFINITION: Tolerance in pressure of expected depth (dbar)
CONF_PARAM_30.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: Defines the pressure threshold (CONFIG_ParkPressure_dbar - CONFIG_PressureThresholdBeforeParkDriftToStopValveAction_dbar) to stop valve action during descent to parking depth.

CONF_PARAM_79.CONF_PARAM_DEFINITION: Volume of SV at surface before considering a grounding (cm3)
CONF_PARAM_79.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: This information is a threshold used to detect a surface grounding of the float. If there is no vertical motion after having tranfered CONFIG_OilVolumeMinForSurfaceGroundingDetection_cm^3 through the valve, the surface gounded flag is activated.

CONF_PARAM_80.CONF_PARAM_LABEL: Volume of SV on descent before considering a grounding (cm3)

CONF_PARAM_80.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: This information is a threshold used to detect a grounding of the float. If there is no vertical motion after having tranfered CONFIG_OilVolumeMinForGroundingDetection_cm^3 through the valve, the gounded flag is activated and the float acts as configurated by the CONFIG_GroundingMode_LOGICAL parameter.So, yes it is a configuration parameter (and I can easily understand that it can be modified via remote control since some PROVOR floats have experienced erroneous grounding detection (under study but perhaps due to in-situ conditions).

CONF_PARAM_114.CONF_PARAM_DESCRIPTION: The pressure at which the CTD pump is switched off.  As the float ascends, the code looks at the pressure and if <= CONFIG_CTDPumpStopPressure, the CTD is turned off. CTDPumpStopPressure is a firmware threshold and as such, data may continue to be collected for a limited span after the threshold is recognized. Especially in floats that return high resolution discrete data, there might be data collected shallower than the cut off, due to the discrete nature of the pressure data and also due to the time necessary for the firmware to turn off the CTD once the pressure threshold is reached. For example for SOLOII floats the CTD is switched off at 1dbar, and typically the shallowest data is from 0.5 to 0.8 dbar. This shallow data should be carefully assessed for its validity.
